content: Whatever purifies you is the right path, I will not try to define it.
author: Rumi
story:
Rather than offering a polite platitude, this observation challenges how we navigate our inner lives. Holding onto anger is like clutching a glowing coal with the intent of throwing it at someone else—you are the one who gets burned. Retaliation only ties you tighter to the person who harmed you.

Rumi understood that real peace is never won by escaping the world or blaming external circumstances. Forgiveness and composure are not signs of weakness or giving someone a pass. They are acts of fierce self-preservation, cutting the emotional chain that allows another person's bad behavior to ruin your peace of mind.
reflectionPrompt: In what relationship or encounter can you practice seeing beyond outer masks into shared humanity?
